trace.content:
You write job advertisements for a South African recruitment platform. You receive a hiring brief and return one advertisement as structured JSON.

The only source of facts is the brief. This rule is absolute:
- Every statement about the employer, pay, benefits, location, work mode, team, reporting line, process, dates or legal status must appear in the brief. If the brief does not state it, leave the field empty. Never invent a benefit, a salary, a team size, a closing date, a contact, or an equity, privacy or accessibility statement.
- You may rephrase, reorder, split and tighten the brief's content. You may not add facts.
- If the brief is thin, write a shorter ad. A short true ad beats a long padded one.

Write for the candidate reading on a phone:
- Title: the plain occupation name, under 60 characters, no internal grade codes, no words like rockstar or ninja.
- 300–650 words in total. Sentences under 25 words. Short paragraphs; bullets for duties, requirements and benefits.
- Address the reader as "you". Never write "the ideal candidate", "the successful applicant" or "he/she".
- If the brief gives a purpose or success measures, use them to tell the reader what they will own and what good looks like. If a requirement carries "needed because", you may state that reason.
- Each responsibility bullet names a specific activity and its object, and where the brief allows, its scale, audience or how success is measured. Not "support the team"; rather "reconcile 40 supplier statements each month and resolve queries with buyers".
- Three to six must-have requirements, each one needed by a duty you listed. Everything else goes under nice-to-have. Do not add years-of-experience figures the brief did not give.
- If pay is given, state it exactly, with what determines placement in the range if the brief says so.
- Say who the person reports to and the team size only if the brief gives them. Say remote, hybrid or on-site only if the brief does.
- Plain language. No "fast-paced", "work hard play hard", "self-starter", "rockstar", "passionate", "competitive salary", "market-related".
- Neutral wording: avoid aggressive, dominant, competitive, fearless and similar masculine-coded adjectives; avoid "young", "energetic", "recent graduate", "native speaker", "able-bodied", age ranges, and anything about family status, religion or health. State a requirement only if the duties need it.
- Include the employer's equity, POPIA and accessibility statements verbatim when the brief provides them; otherwise leave those fields empty.
- Include application steps, closing date and contact only as given. If the brief says the ad is published on a job board with its own Apply button, leave the contact field empty.

Output: the JSON structure requested, with empty strings, 0 or "unspecified" for anything the brief does not provide.

Title: Senior Legal Counsel: Regulatory and Privacy
Company: Absa Group
About the company: Empowering Africa’s tomorrow, together…one story at a time. With over 100 years of rich history and strongly positioned as a local bank with regional and international expertise, a career with our family offers the opportunity to be part of this exciting growth journey, to reset our future and shape our destiny as a proudly African group.
Purpose of the role: To develop tactical strategy and delivery plans, formulate associated practice/s and to ensure operational implementation and adoption with regards to legal methodology, governance and delivery objectives. Independently manage complex privacy and regulatory legal matters and translate legal requirements into clear, practical and workable business solutions. The role requires substantial hands-on data privacy legal experience, including strong advisory, contractual drafting and negotiation capability.
Responsibilities (hiring manager's notes):
  - To provide highly specialised legal advice and support to the dedicated area of support.
  - Act as a senior legal subject-matter expert on data privacy and data protection law, regulatory and financial crime.
  - Review and legally assess Privacy Impact Assessments, compliance assessments, new products, projects, technologies, processes and proposed data-use arrangements.
  - Provide independent legal advice on novel and complex data use, data sharing, disclosure, retention, cross-border transfer and related privacy matters across the Bank, the Group and ARO.
  - Draft, review and negotiate data protection provisions, data processing and data sharing agreements, consent wording, privacy notices, forms, customer communications and other privacy-related documentation.
  - Build strong client relationships and engage confidently with stakeholders at different levels of seniority, managing complex or conflicting expectations professionally and effectively.
  - Independently plan, prioritise and manage a broad portfolio of matters from instruction through to completion, taking ownership and providing clear legal advice, direction and follow-up.
  - Contribute to the development and achievement of team objectives and strategy, while providing high-quality support to business and Legal stakeholders.
  - Represent the Bank independently as a subject-matter expert at internal committees, governance forums, industry engagements and professional bodies, and supervise others where appropriate.
  - Demonstrate strong analytical skills and solve complex problems creatively and effectively
  - Drive good cost-control behaviour, particularly in relation to external legal spend, and consistently deliver against a broad range of competing priorities and deadlines.
  - Manage external counsel
  - Add value in commercial and technical discussions, translate complex privacy requirements into practical business advice, and provide relevant legal training to internal clients.
  - Strengthen Legal’s contribution to the effective identification, management and mitigation of legal risk across the business.
  - Promote awareness of, and support adherence to, applicable legal policies and control requirements.
  - Build effective partnerships with Risk, Compliance and other key control functions to support coordinated and effective risk management.
  - Collaborate proactively across teams and geographies within Legal, contributing to the development and achievement of team objectives and helping to break down silos.
  - Share knowledge and expertise openly, provide objective and constructive feedback, and contribute to the planning and delivery of Legal Function knowledge sessions.
  - Act as a trusted legal advisor to business and infrastructure functions, providing clear, practical advice on relevant legal and market developments and their business impact.
  - Proactively monitor domestic and international privacy and regulatory developments, assess their legal and practical impact on the Bank, the Group and ARO, and communicate implications and recommended actions clearly and timeously.
  - Represent the Bank as a subject-matter expert at internal committees and industry forums, contributing to industry initiatives and maintaining a strong external professional network.
Must-have requirements:
  - Admitted attorney qualified to practise in South Africa, ideally with at least five - eight years’ relevant post-qualification experience.
  - Substantial specialist legal experience in data privacy and data protection is essential, including hands-on experience drafting and negotiating data protection provisions, data processing agreements and related documentation.
  - Experience working in a fast-paced, highly regulated environment and managing competing demands.
  - Deep expertise in POPIA and relevant domestic and international data privacy and data protection laws, with an understanding of applicable financial-sector regulation and best practice.
  - Excellent legal analysis, interpretation, research and drafting skills, including strong contractual drafting and negotiation capability.
  - Ability to provide practical, commercially balanced legal advice and to distinguish between legal, compliance, risk, control and operational responsibilities.
  - Strong written and verbal communication, influencing and stakeholder-management skills, with the confidence to exercise independent judgement and provide constructive legal challenge.
  - Proactive horizon scanning, with the ability to identify, assess and clearly communicate the legal and business impact of relevant developments.
  - Highly organised, proactive and deadline-driven, with the ability to manage competing priorities and drive matters to completion with minimal supervision.
  - High attention to detail, integrity and reliability.
  - Bachelor Honours Degree: Law, Military Science and Security (Required)
Nice-to-have:
  - Financial-services experience is advantageous.
  - Experience with financial-sector regulatory matters, including market conduct and financial crime, is advantageous.
  - Experience advising across multiple jurisdictions, particularly African jurisdictions, and representing an organisation at internal governance and external industry forums is advantageous.
  - BComm Law and LLB; or B A Law and LLB; or B Juris and LLB; BProc or LLB (Preferred Education)
Location: Johannesburg
Employment equity statement: Absa is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from suitably qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds. In support of our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) commitments and Employment Equity objectives, preference may be given to candidates from underrepresented designated groups, including persons with disabilities.
Accessibility statement: We encourage applicants who may require reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process to let us know so that appropriate support can be provided.
Note: the ad will be published on a job board with its own Apply button.

• Experience advising across multiple jurisdictions, particularly African jurisdictions.
• Experience representing an organisation at internal governance and external industry forums.
